articles.standfirst: O levantamento de preços do Guia de Compras revela descontos de até 27% em TVs e eletrodomésticos, mas alerta que 25 dos 74 itens pesquisados estão acima da média.
articles.summary: O levantamento de preços da Black Friday revela descontos de até 27% em TVs e eletrodomésticos, mas alerta que 25 dos 74 itens pesquisados estão acima da média.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Para checar se os preços da Black Friday , nesta sexta (27), têm descontos de verdade, o Guia de Compras pesquisou na última semana como estão os preços de 74 produtos.

No dia da Black Friday, 43 itens ficaram com preços abaixo da média calculada para o período – ou 58% do total. Na quinta (26), eram 45 itens com desconto.

É o segundo maior índice de produtos com valores mais baratos desde o início da varredura diária, na quinta-feira passada (19). O levantamento começou a ser feito em agosto.

Nesta semana, alguns itens chegaram a ficar até duas vezes mais caros em apenas 24 horas.

A alta de descontos é puxada principalmente pelos produtos da marca de eletrodomésticos Hisense , que repetiu o desempenho da quinta (26) e manteve 4 dos seus itens entre os 5 mais baratos.

Veja os produtos com os maiores descontos registrados no início da madrugada de sexta-feira:

TV Hisense Hi-QLED 100Q7QG 100" : 27% abaixo da média (R$ 9.999);

Lava e seca Hisense Serie 3s 12kg/8kg WD3S1243BB1 : 19% abaixo da média (R$ 2.548);

Micro-ondas Panasonic 21L NN-ST27LWRU : 16% abaixo da média (R$ 417);

TV Hisense QLED 55Q7QGPTOBT 55" : 15% abaixo da média (R$ 1.999);

Os valores são referentes ao preço no cartão e não consideram descontos no Pix.

O Guia de Compras vai registrar mais uma varredura de preços no final da manhã de sexta , para verificar se os valores mudaram.

A lista completa com os descontos está na página especial do Guia de Compras.

No total, 13 produtos tiveram quedas a partir de 10% em relação à média do período. A maioria, no entanto, continua com descontos tímidos: 18 itens ficaram abaixo dos 5%.

Por outro lado, 25 dos 74 itens estão mais caros do que a média desde agosto. Da lista, 18 itens tiveram alta entre 1% e 9%, e outros 7, acima de 10%.

É aí que mora o risco: se um produto sobe agora e cai na Black Friday, o “desconto” pode só devolvê-lo ao preço de antes.

É o terceiro ano seguido em que o Guia de Compras faz o levantamento, com base em buscas regulares nas principais lojas da internet. A lista inclui as categorias mais procuradas nesta época, como celulares, TVs, eletrodomésticos, eletroportáteis e videogames.

Na página inicial, você pode visualizar o produto pela faixa de desconto (5%, 10%, 15%) ou selecionar a categoria desejada (ex: Cozinha).

Escolha o modelo do produto em que você procura.

Na página do item, um gráfico de variação de preços mostra rapidamente os momentos em que o produto esteve mais caro e as datas em que atingiu os menores valores.

articles.title: Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. It Was Actually David Fincher Wanting Him in 'Cliff Booth'
articles.summary: The veteran actor reunites with Brad Pitt in the 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood' follow-up that sees him taking on manic 1970s TV star Charlie Peters, who's...
articles.body:
Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. It Was Actually David Fincher Wanting Him in ‘Cliff Booth’

[This story contains spoilers for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .]

Getting battered with warnings about scammer calls and texts is nothing new in today's world. So when Scott Caan got a message, "Hey, David Fincher wants to meet you" for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , understandably he thought, "I'm being punked."

"I was going to write back like, 'Whoever this is, leave me alone.' I thought somebody was playing a joke on me. Yeah, sure, you're texting me to come be in a Fincher movie. Yeah, I believe that for sure," the 50-year-old actor quips when The Hollywood Reporter caught up with him over Zoom just hours before he headed out to the film's U.K. premiere earlier this month.

But it wasn't a joke. The filmmaker's producer partner, Ceán Chaffin, was reaching out about the role of Charlie Peters after Quentin Tarantino — who wrote the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel — and star Brad Pitt suggested Caan for the character.

Given that Tarantino is one of Caan's "favorite writers of all time," and he'd get to reunite with his Ocean's Eleven co-star Pitt, it was an easy yes. But then came the challenging part of taking on a character that "can seem a little crass and insane" on paper, he says, and figuring out, "How do I justify all this?"

Once Pitt's fan-favorite stuntman Cliff Booth gets entangled with Charlie, a popular yet manic 1970s TV star, he realizes he's not being hired as his stunt double, but rather as a fixer to handle a dangerous hitman situation Charlie has found himself in.

"I figure out a way to ground all of it. So none of it seems like an idea or a cliché or a character. I don't want anything to be cartoony," Caan says of how he approached his reckless, unintentionally comedic character on screen. "I want it to be real. And then I got to find a part of myself that is that wild, wild, wild guy."

But as an actor playing an actor, TV superstar Charlie Peters specifically, Caan wasn't just taking a singular role. He also had to embody all of Charlie's characters within the film's fictional shows… talk about a meta experience.

"A lot of people maybe might want to goof on the acting part of it, but David and I talked about it. My goal as Charlie Peters is to win Emmys," he explains, wanting those characters to be as "thorough and lived out and grounded" as anyone else he's portrayed.

Sounds like quite the undertaking, but Caan confesses it's "an actor's fantasy." He adds, "It's a dream to be able to play three or four different characters inside of the movie you've been wanting to make your whole life."

For any actor, Tarantino and Fincher are as high a pedigree creative team as it gets, which only adds to the pressure as a performer.

"I've been doing this for long enough where a lot of the time I go in there, and I feel like I need to help the writing or I need to help, maybe it's a young director," says Caan, who's been a fixture of the industry since the '90s. "Not in an egotistical way, but in a collaborative way." So showing up to set and knowing you're fully taken care of was a "very rare" experience for him.

It also allowed Caan to fully commit to those scenes that will likely have audiences talking for ages, such as Charlie, Cliff and talent agent Karen Crosby's (played by Elizabeth Debicki) first meeting when Cliff suggests Charlie kill a pig as a method acting exercise. Caan's character was understandably bewildered by the thought initially.

"That first scene where we're talking about the pig and he gives me that suggestion … it felt like we were doing a one-act play," the Entourage actor says with excitement in his voice. "As far as fun, and we did that scene a lot of times, I've never gone home and felt like, wow, that was… I never felt anything like that. We just did a one-act play 50 times today, and full 10-minute takes of that scene, and it's all over the place."

That was only the beginning of Cliff and Charlie's chaotic journey that would unfold across the next hour, but for one unfortunate piggy, it would soon be the end, as Charlie takes Cliff's acting advice quite literally. In a moment of symbolism, it's "really the beginning of my nervous breakdown," Caan says of his once-confident character now panicking, drenched in pig's blood towards the end.

"This scene, it has to work. If this scene doesn't work, then the Charlie journey is not complete," he explains. "So I remember being really, really, really sad all day long, just trying to stay in a really upset place, and Fincher was paying attention, and he just had me do it again and again and again until we were exhausted. It was a very memorable day of shooting."

While Cliff goes on to do Charlie's dirty work for him in the final showdown with the hitmen, Caan's character is left "having to deal with all of my demons, digging deep and sorting out all my trauma" that's got him to this point, he says.

Similar to how Charlie's storyline ends with a moment of reflection, that's also how Caan walked away from the movie, having wrapped his first collaboration with Fincher and Tarantino. "I wish we could start over right now," he admits.

The film also serves as the first major project Caan worked on following the death of his father and Hollywood icon James Caan in 2022 . Known for his intense, charismatic performances, Scott's Cliff Booth performance undoubtedly felt like a nod to his legacy.

"I think about him every day anyway, let alone when I'm going into doing something that I think that he would've appreciated, something that he would've been great in," he says of his dad.

But Caan is also working to build a Hollywood legacy of his own, one that already includes dozens of roles from energetic getaway driver Turk Malloy in the Ocean's Eleven franchise (and yes, he's "100 percent" down to reprise his role in Ocean's 14 ) to Detective Danny Williams in the Hawaii Five-0 reboot. And now, Charlie Peters in Cliff Booth and agent Nick Schaeffer in NCIS: New York .

Even with a stacked resume, Caan feels he's still not in a place in his career where he can be too picky about the opportunities that come his way, especially in an industry with a limited — and shrinking — number of jobs.

"I think we all would like to think that we're at a point in our career where we can pick and choose, but the truth of the matter is, I feel like when I was younger, I felt that way," he admits. "And as I get older and have been in the business for a long time, you're just kind of lucky to be working."

So when you get a text that Fincher wants to cast you in a film written by Tarantino, naturally it's going to feel pretty surreal, even for a veteran like Caan. Because even after decades in the business, he tells THR , "I'm just constantly trying to figure out what I want to be when I grow up, and I'm still doing that, and that's the fun of our business."

He quips with a laugh, "I'm still only in my 20s. I got a ways to go, you know what I mean?"

articles.title: Aryan Khan's rumoured girlfriend Larissa Bonesi says he is intelligent and determined, the Khans are like family to her: 'Shah Rukh Khan is the King, will be number one forever'
articles.summary: Brazilian model and actress Larissa Bonesi has described the Khan family as her own, speaking about her bond with actor Shah Rukh Khan and his son,
articles.body: Brazilian model and actress Larissa Bonesi has described the Khan family as her own, speaking about her bond with actor Shah Rukh Khan and his son, filmmaker Aryan Khan. Larissa and Aryan are often spotted together, which lead to the speculation that they are in a relationship. They have not commented on the rumours publicly.Larissa Bonesi, who moved to India 16 years ago and now considers Mumbai home, said her admiration for the Khans comes from both their achievements and who they are as people. She described their support as something that means a great deal to her and said the friendship she shares with the family goes a long way. Talking about her bonding, she told Bombay Times, "The Khans are like family. When you admire people for what they have achieved in life, have respect for them, and how they are as human beings, you kind of feel that they are family. Their support means a lot. Friendship is everything, and it is something that goes a long way.”While talking about Shah Rukh Khan, Larissa Bonesi was all praise. “He is the King. He is a legend, and he is going to be number one forever. There is so much to learn from him. It is not just about being famous or what you have achieved, but also about how you did it. He is someone you look up to,” she said in a conversation with Bombay Times.She was equally specific in her praise for Aryan Khan, who made his directorial debut with the web series The Bastards of Bollywood. “Aryan is a great person. He is intelligent and determined. Sometimes people say, ‘But he has everything.’ However, he does not care about that. He is fighting for what he wants, he is fighting for his future and for the things he believes in. He will get there because he is a very determined guy,” she said. Larissa Bonesi added that she visited the sets of Aryan’s show once and would love to be directed by him someday, saying anyone would want to work with someone that talented.While her friendships have helped her build a life in Mumbai, Larissa Bonesi acknowledged that navigating the Indian entertainment industry as a foreigner has not always been straightforward. She said there have been ups and downs, and that entering the industry from outside the country was difficult at first. Over time, she adapted to her circumstances and found acceptance from both the public and the people around her.On the professional front, Larissa Bonesi said she is looking forward to her upcoming horror film 1920: Cold Winter. She described herself as a fan of the horror genre and said the role was the kind she had been waiting for. "I think there's some women that I'm really developing strong feelings for, and I'm excited to continue this journey with them," he said. "Today I chose Kylee. While speaking to Cates, Kylee shared more about her faith and revealed she previously appeared on "The Bachelor." She explained that after her time on that show, she still "believe[s] in environments like this," but noted that she got "burned." articles.title: Gérard Depardieu Rape Case Sent To Trial In Criminal Court After Actor Loses Appeal
articles.summary: Gérard Depardieu will stand trial in a criminal court on a rape charge related to accusations by actress Charlotte Arnould, after an appeal by his lawyers fa...
articles.body:
Gérard Depardieu will stand trial in a criminal court on a rape charge related to accusations by actress Charlotte Arnould, after an appeal by his lawyers failed.

The Paris Court of Appeal said on Thursday that Depardieu would be tried for one part of the accusations levelled by Arnould against the actor.

The actress, whose father was an old friend of the actor, accuses Depardieu of raping and sexually assaulting her twice in his Paris mansion in the summer of 2018 after she went to him for acting advice.

The court has ruled that Depardieu will be tried for the first alleged rape on August 7, 2018, but not the second alleged rape on August 13, due to insufficient evidence.

The decision to proceed with the trail comes eight months after Depardieu was found guilty of sexual assault and given an 18-month suspended sentence related to events on the set of Jean Becker's The Green Shutters in 2021.

The acto r last week announced he was abandoning plans to appeal the sentence and issued a statement saying that he recognized his culpability and apologized for the hurt he had caused.

Just days after the letter was published, investigative newsite Mediapart published details of a fresh sexual assault and rape complaint against the actor related to events on the shoot of Guillaume Nicloux's Thalasso in 2018.

His 18-month suspended sentence related to assaults on two female crew members on the set of The Green Shutters .

A number of women, who were not pressing charges, also gave evidence at the trial, including an actress who alleged Depardieu had shoved his hands into her knickers during a photo-call on the set of Netflix show Marseille .

Arnould was the first woman to pursue Depardieu in the courts in relation to sexual assault allegations, but her move came against a backdrop of growing rumors around the actor's sexually inappropriate treatment of female extras and crew members on film sets.

Her complaint was initially dismissed by the courts following a nine-month investigation for lack of evidence, but she filed a second complaint as a civil party, which resulted in an investigating judge being appointed in 2020, and Depardieu being indicted for rape and sexual assault in 2021.

In between times, Depardieu's public star plummeted following an exposé of his alleged sexual misconduct by state broadcaster channel France 2's investigative show Complément d'Enquête , entitled "The fall of the ogre", which aired in December 2023.

The allegations and 2026 guilty verdict have brought his acting career to a grinding halt. Since 2022, he has worked on only three productions, one of them directed by his longtime friend Fanny Ardant.

The criminal court is France's highest level of court reserved for crimes carrying sentences of more than five years, if the accused is found guilty.

articles.title: Khloé Kardashian admits she’s open to marrying gay man after 5 years without sex: ‘Depends what that gay man can do for me’
articles.summary: “Like, will you make me look pretty every day? Sold. That’s all it takes,” Kardashian said amid her celibacy journey.
articles.body:
Reality TV star Khloe Kardashian admitted she's open to marrying a gay man after five years of celibacy.

Kardashian and influencer Colt Paulsen discussed "lavender marriage" on The Kardashians .

"I mean, it depends what that gay man can do for me. Like, will you make me look pretty every day?" she asked.

Khloé Kardashian (maybe) wants a lavender kind of love!

After revealing earlier this month that she's demisexual amid a five-year celibacy journey, the reality TV icon said she's open to marrying a gay man 10 years after her divorce from Lamar Odom and five years after splitting from ex-boyfriend Tristan Thompson.

"You need a man, all your sisters are dating," influencer Colt Paulsen told Kardashian on the latest episode of Hulu's The Kardashians series.

He then suggested, "You can always do the lavender marriage. If you ever need, I'm here," to which Kardashain replied, "Oh, yeah. Well, that? I'm down with anytime!"

The show then defined via title card what exactly a "lavender marriage" is, with the program's text describing it as "a marriage of convenience between a man and a woman where one or both is queer."

In a confessional, the 42-year-old elaborated on her thoughts about lavender marriages — including if one would ever be the right fit for her at this stage of her life while raising two children.

"Would I have a lavender marriage? There's times, yes, and then other times, I'm like, to take care of one more person? I don't know," she admitted.

She continued: "I mean, it depends what that gay man can do for me. Like, will you make me look pretty every day? Sold. That's all it takes!"

Kardashian and Odom divorced in 2016 after seven years of marriage, while the dissolution of her relationship with Thompson led to her ongoing celibacy journey.

On a recent episode of her Khloé in Wonder Land podcast, Kardashian came to the realization that she's demisexual , which means that a person can only achieve physical intimacy after establishing an emotional connection with another person.

"It's just really hard for me to be in that headspace right now, like that I want to just even lean into someone, because I just feel like so much has happened," Kardashian explained. "I'm in such a good place that I'm afraid to ever do something that might ever turn out the way that my past has been. Do you know what I mean?"

articles.title: Kelsey Grammer calls American Dream a ‘gift’ he wants to pass down to his 8 children
articles.summary: Kelsey Grammer says the American Dream is a "gift" that he wants to pass down to his eight children as he marks the United States' 250th anniversary with "The America Opus."
articles.body: Kelsey Grammer believes the American Dream is alive and well, and the "Frasier" star is determined to make sure his eight children understand the freedom and opportunity that come with it. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 71-year-old actor reflected on the values he hopes to instill in his children as the United States of America celebrates its 250th anniversary, and he helps commemorate the nation's history through the collector's book "The America Opus." "The thing I most want to pass down to them is the understanding that it's your job. Your gift is the American Dream," Grammer said. "What it entails is up to you." KELSEY GRAMMER WARNS OF CHILLING DANGER FACING AMERICANS WHO FORGET NATION'S FOUNDING HISTORY "Every individual has the same right to figure out what that dream is and to make it happen," he added. The "Cheers" alum shared his view that the American Dream is not just about achieving personal success, but also about having the opportunity to make a difference. WATCH: KELSEY GRAMMER ON WHAT HE WANTS HIS 8 CHILDREN TO LEARN: 'YOUR GIFT IS THE AMERICAN DREAM' Grammer pointed to Alexander Graham Bell as an example of someone who made his American Dream a reality while helping others, noting that the inventor's efforts to help deaf children communicate eventually led to the development of the telephone. "My hat is off to people who end up thinking of something that millions of people need. Why wouldn't we allow those people success? Why wouldn't we praise them? Sort of laud them as being the examples of how wonderful America is," Grammer said. "These people are all American heroes by virtue of the fact that they kept working at their dream," he continued. "Their dream was to help somebody. And it ended up helping millions of people." When asked how he hopes his children will remember him beyond his Hollywood career, Grammer emphasized the importance of setting an example through hard work and personal responsibility. THE FOUNDING FATHERS GAVE US AMERICA. 250 YEARS LATER, WE STILL DEPEND ON GOOD DADS "I hope they look on me as a guy who was incredibly fair. Firm. I have high expectations of people, I expect people to show up," he said. "Because I do. One of my sayings that I say to people is like, if I've got a job being done around the house and I haven't seen the guys for a few weeks, I say, 'You know, if I did my job this way, I wouldn't have this house, I wouldn't have anything else.' "You gotta show up," Grammer continued. "That's the big thing. Your American Dream actually is in your hands. I mean, and I do say this to a lot of people these days, I say like, 'Anybody tells you the American Dream's over, don't give them your vote because that's what they want. They want it over. Theirs is that it's over.' You know, no thanks." Grammer, who has been married four times, shares his eldest child, daughter Spencer Grammer, 43, with his first wife, Doreen Alderman. He is also father to daughter Greer Grammer, 34, whom he shares with his ex-girlfriend Barrie Buckner. The "Grand Isle" actor has daughter Mason Olivia, 25, and son Jude Gordon, 22, with his ex-wife Camille Grammer, 54. He married British former flight attendant Kayte Walsh in 2011. Grammer and Walsh are parents to daughter Faith Evangeline, 14, and sons Kelsey Gabriel, 12, Auden James, 10, and Christopher, 1. articles.title: Before Sai Pallavi's casting as Sita sparked criticism, Shobhna Samarth called the 'OG Sita' by granddaughter Kajol faced backlash for playing the goddess while being eight months pregnant in 'Raambaan'
articles.summary: Long before Sai Pallavi's casting as Sita in Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana' sparked discussions, another actress faced severe criticism for playing the
articles.body: Long before Sai Pallavi's casting as Sita in Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana' sparked discussions, another actress faced severe criticism for playing the revered character on screen. Shobhna Samarth, whom her granddaughter Kajol has fondly referred to as the 'OG Sita', found herself at the centre of a controversy during the making of the 1948 film 'Raambaan'. The reason was that she was eight months pregnant while portraying the goddess.The issue drew a particularly sharp response from FilmIndia editor Baburao Patel, who objected to Shobhna playing Sita while expecting a child. In his review of the film, Patel argued that her pregnancy was incompatible with the idealised image of the goddess."Her pregnancy stares everyone in the eye and becomes a sickly and sacrilegious spectacle through 14147 feet of the film. It is contrary to the spirit of loftiness and sublimity associated with the name of Sita to ask a woman in her dangerously delicate situation to play a role which is worshipped by millions as the noblest and divine ideal of a woman," he wrote.Patel's criticism also extended to Shobhna's appearance. He questioned whether she was suited to portray Sita, making pointed remarks about her age and physical features."Apart from this problem of pregnancy, Shobhna, as the mother of several children, looks too old and emaciated a woman, with sunken cheeks, bulging anaemic eyes, shapeless arms and sagging hips to portray Sita," he added.The review went beyond criticising the casting, with Patel even urging Hindu audiences to boycott the film. He maintained that showing a visibly pregnant Shobhna as Sita could give young viewers the impression that the goddess was pregnant during her exile.The controversy was especially striking given the actress's earlier success in the role. Shobhna had first portrayed Sita in Vijay Bhatt's 'Bharat Milap' (1942), which depicted the events surrounding Ram, Sita and Lakshman's exile from Ayodhya. Following the film's success, Bhatt reunited the cast for 'Ram Rajya' in 1943, which further cemented Shobhna's association with the character.'Ram Rajya' also holds a notable place in Indian cinema history. Mahatma Gandhi, who was known to have little interest in films, is believed to have watched Vijay Bhatt's film, making it the only movie he saw during his lifetime.However, the same success did not follow with 'Raambaan', which arrived in 1948. The film traced the events leading up to Sita's abduction by Ravana, including Lakshman's encounter with Shurpanakha and Ram and Lakshman's alliance with Hanuman and Sugriva.Despite having earned recognition for her earlier portrayals of Sita, Shobhna's casting in 'Raambaan' became a subject of intense debate, with her pregnancy drawing criticism that went far beyond a discussion of her performance.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Priyanka Chopra pays tribute to the victims and martyrs of the 26/11 Mumbai attacks: 'Remembering the lives lost and the heroes who gave everything on 26/11'
articles.summary: Priyanka Chopra and Bhumi Pednekar have paid emotional tributes to the victims and brave defenders of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks on its anniversary.
articles.body: Priyanka Chopra and Bhumi Pednekar have paid emotional tributes to the victims and brave defenders of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks on its anniversary. While Priyanka shared a short note on Instagram, Bhumi spoke to the media about the strength and unity of the nation.Priyanka Chopra's Instagram tributePriyanka Chopra honoured the lives lost and the security personnel who risked everything to protect citizens. She posted on her Instagram Stories, "Remembering the lives lost and the heroes who gave everything on 26/11."Bhumi Pednekar calls it an attack on IndiaBhumi Pednekar, who was born in Mumbai, described the day in 2008 as "a dark day which halted the city". The 'Dum Laga Ke Haisha' actress thanked those who stood firm during the crisis and said the city holds a special place in her heart.The 'Pati Patni Aur Woh' star said, “I would like to say that all our martyrs, Mumbai police officers, our armed forces, survivors, frontline responders, and all the citizens of Mumbai who have spent such a dark day, and I am also from Mumbai, I was born here, I have Mumbai in my heart. I think the attack on 26/11 was not only on Mumbai, but on our country”.Bhumi also spoke about the spirit of the country and the importance of remembering those affected. She added, “But the most beautiful thing about our country is that wherever we see hatred, we will turn it into love; we will turn it into hope. And even today, where we remember all those martyrs, we remember all those people who lost their lives, their families, I bow my head and say that your stories, what happened to you, will never be forgotten. And we will fill the world with so much love that there will be no place for hatred. There will be no space for terrorism in the world."What happened on November 26, 2008On that day, ten Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists based in Pakistan carried out coordinated strikes across Mumbai. Their targets included the Taj Hotel, the Oberoi, CST, Leopold Cafe and Nariman House, among other places. The siege lasted 60 hours and left 166 people dead and 238 injured.Security forces killed nine of the ten attackers. articles.summary: Gerard Depardieu will stand trial in the alleged 2018 rape of Charlotte Arnould, who says the French actor assaulted her in his Paris home when she was 22.
articles.body: French actor Gerard Depardieu will stand trial in the alleged 2018 rape of actress Charlotte Arnould, Depardieu's lawyer David-Olivier Kaminski told reporters Thursday. Arnould accused the 77-year-old Depardieu of raping her in 2018 when she was 22 and he was 70. She claims he assaulted her in his Paris home. Depardieu, a veritable star of French cinema, has faced numerous sexual assault claims in recent years. In May 2025, a Paris court found him guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set and ordered that he be added to France's national sex offender registry. CATE BLANCHETT MOURNS HOW #METOO GOT 'KILLED VERY QUICKLY,' STILL 'SYSTEMIC LAYER OF ABUSE' Depardieu initially appealed the ruling, but dropped his appeal in mid-November. "I have come to understand that I belonged to a world that no longer exists," he said, adding, "I have therefore decided to withdraw my appeal." Depardieu also apologized and said, "On film sets, I have long hidden behind provocation and crude humor. I believed my words and some of my actions had no consequences. But they did, particularly coming from someone who held as much power as I once did." Despite appearing to acknowledge his behavior was inappropriate in the 2025 case, Depardieu has denied any wrongdoing in the Arnould case. GERARD DEPARDIEU SPEAKS OUT, MAINTAINS INNOCENCE AFTER BEING CHARGED FOR RAPE AND SEXUAL ASSAULT In a 2023 op-ed in French newspaper Le Figaro, Depardieu wrote, "Never, ever have I abused a woman. To harm a woman would be like kicking my own mother in the stomach." In the essay, he claimed, "A woman came to my house once, walking lightly, going up to my room of her own accord. She now says she was raped there. She returned there a second time. There has never been any coercion, violence, or protest between us." Arnould, in a social media post shortly after the letter became public, called it "a truly vile message." "He positions himself as the victim to elicit compassion and sow doubt. To put things in context, when I went to his place, I was 22 years old, I weighed 37 kilos because I suffered from anorexia, and he was a friend of my father's," she told Elle magazine. The young actress and aspiring dancer also added that "at no point did I consent." Arnould's attorney, Carine Durrieu-Diebolt, also said that she was "shocked and scandalized" at Depardieu's letter. Delphine Meillet, another attorney representing Depardieu, told The Associated Press that he disputes the ruling to proceed with his case, though he did not specify if he plans to appeal. articles.title: 'One Job Away' campaign is helping SAG-AFTRA members meet work thresholds to keep health insurance
articles.summary: Actor Cheyenne Jackson’s “One Job Away" campaign helping fellow SAG-AFTRA members meet work thresholds to maintain health insurance
articles.body: A grassroots social media campaign led by actor and singer Cheyenne Jackson has helped fellow SAG-AFTRA members struggling during declining film and TV production earn enough to keep their union health insurance. Jackson, known for his roles in "American Horror Story," "30 Rock" and "Glee," launched the "One Job Away" movement on Instagram last month to spotlight fellow performers struggling to earn enough to maintain medical coverage through the Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists. SAG-AFTRA requires members to earn at least $28,000 annually to qualify for health insurance, with four quarterly deadlines for meeting that threshold, depending on when they joined the union. NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE' For actors working job to job, meeting that requirement has become increasingly difficult as U.S. film and TV production contracts and healthcare costs rise. "So the success of the project so far at last count is that eight actors have been hired directly and at least 12 to 15 have been pinned or called back or gotten really close," Jackson told Fox News Digital. He described an overwhelming response, including hundreds of direct messages from actors hoping to be featured, many of whom are just a few hundred dollars short of qualifying. Among them is William Ngo, who was born and raised in Southern California but relocated to Philadelphia after work dried up following the pandemic and the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike. Ngo, whose credits include The CW’s "The Vampire Diaries," HBO Max’s "The Staircase" and Apple’s "Bad Monkey," is just $500 short of qualifying for SAG-AFTRA health insurance. Actress and stunt performer Marie Gibeault, whose credits include Netflix’s "The Four Seasons" and multiple commercials, is only $800 short of qualifying. Navy veteran, actor and voice-over artist Jonathan Medina needs one guest role to qualify by the end of the year. ROB RIGGLE SAYS HOLLYWOOD WORK IS DISAPPEARING FROM LA: 'IT'S THE EXCEPTION NOW' Actor Alejandro Cardenas reached out to thank Jackson after the campaign helped him book a small role that put him over the earnings threshold. "After Cheyenne posted my picture and info, an executive from Lionsgate and friend of mine immediately called me and set me up into this job so I could make the money needed to reach the minimum to qualify for my health insurance again," Cardenas told Fox News Digital from the set he was working on in New Jersey. The actors’ profiles share a common thread: dwindling opportunities in Hollywood during fewer scripted television orders, increased cost-cutting and the continued shift of production elsewhere. TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS Jackson previously described the industry’s struggles as "systemic" during an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. "People that have been leads of television shows have worked for years and years and years, and you know their faces, and you know their work. This year, they’re like, ‘What am I going to do?’" he said. Meanwhile, beginning Jan. 1, quarterly premiums and earnings thresholds are expected to rise by 1%, with additional annual increases of 1% to follow, according to terms negotiated in SAG-AFTRA’s latest contract with streamers and studios. A petition calling for an audit of the union’s health plan has also gained traction among members. SAG-AFTRA, which represents approximately 170,000 media professionals worldwide, has faced criticism over the nearly $1.1 million annual salary of its national executive director and chief negotiator, Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, as members struggle financially. Fox News Digital reached out to SAG-AFTRA’s chief communications and marketing officer, Pamela Greenwalt, for comment. In response, a union representative provided a healthcare fact sheet and a membership termination sheet. Jackson, who also performs onstage, has expressed a desire to discuss how the system works, noting that actors can have a strong earnings year followed by a lean one that leaves them ineligible for health benefits. He told Fox News Digital that launching "One Job Away" was a way to pass along kindness he had received. Last year, for the first time in his 20-year career, Jackson found himself $6,000 short of meeting the health insurance eligibility requirements. Actress Kathy Bates, who had worked with him on "American Horror Story," arranged for him to have four speaking lines on her CBS series "Matlock." The work was enough to qualify him and his family for coverage. "I really did nothing," Jackson said of launching "One Job Away." He added that several peers, including actresses Jamie Lee Curtis and Sarah Paulson, have reached out to ask how they can help. articles.summary: El periodista de La Sexta ha hablado en los Premios Ondas con un mensaje para movilizar a los electores al 29N
articles.body: La gala de los Premios Ondas volvió a convertirse un año más en un escaparate para la ironía y la mirada crítica sobre el ecosistema mediático español. Entre aplausos y risas del público, Jordi Évole aprovechó el micrófono para lanzar un alegato en clave de humor sobre la relación entre la actualidad política, la televisión y las jornadas electorales, recordando que "El domingo hay unas elecciones y hay que ir a votar. Y yo sé el tipo de gente que se junta en los Ondas". Con ese punto de partida cómplice, el comunicador pidió a los asistentes que miraran más allá de la ceremonia y pensaran en el esfuerzo sostenido de determinados rostros de la comunicación. "Entonces, os quiero pedir que penséis en vuestros compañeros y compañeras que llevan cuatro años dándolo todo para que caiga este Gobierno", señaló, invitando a la sala a poner nombres y apellidos a esa idea. En su enumeración, Évole citó de forma directa a figuras muy reconocidas del panorama mediático y de la tertulia política. "Pensad en ellos, que se os pase por la cabeza, yo qué sé, Iker (Jiménez), Pablo (Motos), Antonio (Ferreras), Carmen (Porter), Ana Rosa (Quintana)... pensad en todos ellos y sobre todo también pensad en Eduardo Inda. Acordaros de él el domingo". El tono satírico alcanzó su punto culminante cuando el presentador vinculó el resultado de las urnas con el estado de ánimo de esos comunicadores al día siguiente. "No les demos un mal lunes. Esta gente lleva mucho tiempo dándolo todo para que esto cambie. No les demos un mal lunes, por favor", añadió ante la reacción de los presentes. Évole cerró su intervención con una frase de aparente recomendación que arrancó una reacción en el auditorio, resumiendo con sorna el espíritu de su mensaje. "El domingo si os podéis quedar en casa, mejor. ¡Venga! ¡Hostia, sí se puede!", remató el periodista para concluir su intervención.

articles.title: French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial on  2018 rape charge: Lawyer
articles.summary: French actor Gerard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, one of his lawyers told The
articles.body: French actor Gerard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, one of his lawyers told The Associated Press on Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.Defense lawyer Delphine Meillet wrote in a message to the AP that the 77-year-old actor would face trial over only one of the two alleged rapes reported by actress Charlotte Arnould.Depardieu, who has denied the rape allegations, had challenged an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send him to trial.The Paris Court of Appeal upheld that decision Thursday in relation to one of the two alleged rapes."He disputes the decision," Meillet told AP, without specifying whether Depardieu would file a further appeal.Arnould first lodged a complaint in 2018, when she was 22. The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.A French cinema icon faces a #MeToo reckoningFor half a century, Depardieu was a towering figure in French cinema.With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, he became one of the country's most recognizable cultural exports, earning an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card."But accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.Earlier this month, Depardieu dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021, accepting an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issuing a public apology."I was found guilty," Depardieu said in a written statement on Nov. 16, adding that he accepted the sentence."I therefore offer my deep and sincere apologies to those who may have suffered," he said.Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 of groping a set decorator and an assistant during the filming of "Les Volets Verts" ("The Green Shutters"). The case was widely seen as a test of the French film industry's response to the #MeToo movement."On film sets, I have long hidden behind provocation and crude humor. I believed my words and some of my actions had no consequences. But they did, particularly coming from someone who held as much power as I once did," Depardieu said in his statement.Accusations against Depardieu sparked a national debateDepardieu's behavior toward women came under renewed scrutiny in December 2023 after a television documentary showed him repeatedly making obscene remarks and gestures during a 2018 trip to North Korea.French President Emmanuel Macron drew criticism from women's rights activists at the time when he defended Depardieu, saying the actor "makes France proud."Macron invoked the presumption of innocence and said he would not participate in a "manhunt."The controversy exposed divisions in France over the #MeToo movement.In 2018, actress Catherine Deneuve and 99 other women signed an open letter defending men's freedom to pursue women and warning against what they saw as the movement's excesses.Born in 1948 into a working-class family in the central French city of Chateauroux, Depardieu overcame a speech impediment to become one of France's most prolific actors.His career spanned hundreds of films, including "The Last Metro," "Jean de Florette" and the popular "Asterix" franchise.His excesses off-screen also made international headlines, notably when he accepted a Russian passport from President Vladimir Putin in 2013 amid a dispute over French taxes.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Ramayana’ box office collection Day 22: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer wraps up third week with Rs 128 crore haul; epic set to cross Rs 1,000 crore net milestone
articles.summary: ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, has concluded another successful week at the box office.
articles.body: ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, has concluded another successful week at the box office. The film wrapped up its third week at the Indian box office with a net collection of Rs 9.65 crore.As per the latest report on sacnilk, the film fell a tad short of the Rs 10 crore mark on Thursday, but with its collections, managed to push its total India net collection to Rs 992.10 crore. With this, the mythological epic is now just Rs 7.90 crore away from entering the Rs 1,000 crore domestic net club. The film's total India gross collection now stands at Rs 1,185 crore.The latest box office figures indicate that the Hindi version contributed the bulk of Thursday's collections, earning Rs 6.75 crore from 13,287 shows. The Malayalam version collected Rs 1 crore, while the Kannada version added Rs 85 lakh and the Tamil version earned Rs 75 lakh, followed by Telugu with Rs 30 lakh.‘Ramayana’ box office: Week-wise collectionsThe film witnessed a strong opening week, collecting Rs 564.60 crore net and Rs 675.05 crore gross between Days 1 and 8. In its second week, the film scored another Rs 299.15 crore net and Rs 357.10 crore gross. Its third week total of Rs 128.35 crore net and Rs 152.85 crore gross has thus helped the film make its way to the Rs 1000 crore mark.‘Ramayana’ worldwide box office collectionOverseas, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer collected an estimated Rs 10 crore on Day 22, taking its cumulative international gross to Rs 592 crore. This takes its worldwide gross collection to Rs 1,777 crore, with its domestic gross standing at Rs 1,185 crore.'Ramayana' becomes fourth Indian film to cross Rs 1,800 crore markIn just its third week, 'Ramayana' is just inches away from crossing the Rs 1,800 crore mark at the box office. With this, it will become only the fourth Indian film to hit the milestone, after 'Dangal' (2016), 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge' (2026), and 'Baahubali 2: The Conclusion'.‘Ramayana’ inches closer to Rs 1,000 crore India net milestoneFor nearly seven years, SS Rajamouli's ‘Baahubali 2: The Conclusion’ remained the only Indian film to cross the Rs 1,000 crore net mark at the domestic box office, until ‘Pushpa 2: The Rule’ joined the club in December 2024. Earlier this year, ‘Dhurandhar 2’ became the first Bollywood film to achieve the milestone.Now, ‘Ramayana’ is on the verge of becoming the second Bollywood production to enter the exclusive Rs 1,000 crore India net club. With its current domestic net collection at Rs 992.10 crore, the film is only a few crore short on hitting the milestone.Based on its current box office trend, the film could achieve the milestone on Day 23, Friday, November 27, provided it maintains sufficient momentum.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Music at Oxford launches first mini South Asian culture festival
articles.summary: Your guide to a weekend of events at an "authentic South Asian experience" in Oxford.
articles.body:
A music charity is staging its first "mini festival" celebrating South Asian culture.

Music at Oxford kicks off in the city later and will feature tabla playing, dance workshops, music from the Sufi tradition and an Indian film screening.

Artistic and executive director, Rebecca Dawson, said the short weekend-long festival format gave people a chance to learn more about the culture at venues including the Sheldonian Theatre.

Dawson said all the concerts would have special decoration, lighting and amplification to make for "a really, really authentic South Asian experience".

Ssarod virtuoso Soumik Datta and his band will opening the event on Friday at the Sheldonian, with the final concert in their UK tour, Melodies in Slow Motion.

Saturday will feature a workshop and performance by UK-based tabla maestro Shahbaz Hussain , Bollywood and Gujarati dancing with Pooja Rajguru and a family-friendly rave with DJ Indy at the St Clement's Centre.

Singer Chahat Mahmood Ali Qawwal and his musicians will play music from the Sufi tradition at St Mary Magdalen.

On Sunday, researcher, writer and dancer Dr Ranjini Nair will give a talk at the Asian Cultural Centre.

The Jacqueline du Pré Music Building at St Hilda's College will host a screening of 2010 film Natarang and a "diverse fusion of Indian classical music and jazz" by Tabla For Two.

Dawson said some of the group's musicians had been University of Oxford students.

Trina Banerjee, who will be performing with the group, said she was "super excited, honoured and privileged to be a part of the festival".

Dawson said there was "a real thirst" for South Asian music locally: "We did three concerts previously ... and they were just so popular."

She said she found South Asian music "really virtuosic" and "exciting".

"I remember at the end of one concert last year, the musicians just played faster and faster - it was just incredible to watch how they did it," she said.

"We are moving now to a business model where we're going to do more mini festivals, looking at all kinds of different music around the world."

articles.title: Jamie Lee Curtis talks about ‘like Dolly and says she will be welcoming, gentle and generous’ for this Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Join Jamie Lee Curtis this Thanksgiving in embracing kindness, generosity, and acceptance while reflecting on her personal milestones and celebrating the spirit of community inspired by Dolly Parton.
articles.body: Jamie Lee Curtis is urging people to rise above their rigid judgments, selfishness, and negativity and is telling them to embrace kindness, generosity, and acceptance, among other things this Thanksgiving season. Taking to her social media account, the famed veteran actress also remembered Dolly Parton and commented on how people should be more like her as well. Read ahead to know more about what the actress had to share.Jamie Lee Curtis talks about how we should all be like Dolly PartonCurtis celebrated Thanksgiving this year and also her 68th birthday on November 22. Taking to her Instagram account, the actress talked about how she is logging off to take a break from the hate and judgment around her. She also urged people to be more like Dolly Parton as well.Her post read, “Going to turn off the noise for a moment. To all out there in this vast environment that we opt into, if you're lucky enough to have one, the Thanksgiving meal is not hard. It's a roasted bird and potatoes. What's hard are the people with their binary and rigid ideas and judgments and petty selfishness. Today let's all be like Dolly and be welcoming and gentle and generous.”The caption was added along with a photo of Curtis overlooking the sea while stretching her legs on the railings that she was leaning on. The comment section was filled to the brim with people sharing heart emojis and talking about how they completely agree with her.Jamie Lee Curtis’ birthday postEarlier this week, on November 22, Curtis talked about her 68th birthday and commented on how she is one of the last surviving members of her family now. She wrote, “Today will be the first year that I am the only surviving family member of my immediate family and my immediate second family. The last in the line.”She added photos of her parents, Mom Janet Leigh and Dad Tony Curtis, as well as her sister, Kelly Lee Curtis, all of whom have passed away. After facing some criticism over her birthday post, she again posted a lengthy message on November 24. This message read, “Oh my goodness, Internet. Really? Is it such a slow news cycle that you have to turn this into a beef or me throwing shade? Come on. You know better than that. Or do you? Immediate family means my immediate family. My mother and my father and my sister Kelly and my stepfather, who raised me.”She also mentioned that she is in close contact with all of her extended family members and that people should not turn this into something that is not just for the sake of ‘clickbait.’Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh explores Mumbai’s food scene ahead of Aura India Tour concert; enjoys Maharashtrian, Parsi, Gujarati and South Indian delicacies
articles.summary: Punjabi star singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh seems to be soaking in the flavours of Mumbai ahead of his much-awaited concert in the city.
articles.body: Punjabi star singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh seems to be soaking in the flavours of Mumbai ahead of his much-awaited concert in the city.He was seen indulging in a variety of regional thalis and local favourites as he prepared to take the stage for his Aura India Tour show.Diljit, who is known for his love for food and often gives fans a glimpse into his culinary adventures, and this time around, explored an assortment of Indian cuisines during his Mumbai stay. His food trail included authentic Mumbai and Parsi fare, along with Gujarati and South Indian dishes.Among the spread was a traditional Mumbai thali, featuring popular city's favourites such as vada pav. He was also introduced to a homemade chutney along with fafda, khandvi etc.The singer also sampled Parsi cuisine, including a Parsi cutlet, pav with chutney and the much-loved keema pav. Going through the spread, Diljit particularly expressed his fondness for the cutlet.The food experience also took him through South Indian flavours, with a thali comprising idli, dosa, vada, four varieties of chutney, poori and upma.The culinary experience reflected the multi-diverse essence of Mumbai, where Maharashtrian, Gujarati, Parsi and South Indian food traditions have long been part of the city's diverse food culture.Diljit is currently in Mumbai for the India leg of his ongoing Aura World Tour. The Mumbai concert is scheduled to take place on Friday, November 27.Ahead of the concert, Diljit was also making the most of his downtime in the city. articles.title: Kolkata to Experience an Enchanting Sufi Qawwali Evening with A.R. Rahman’s KM Sufi Ensemble
articles.summary: Bringing the richness of India’s musical heritage to the city, Once Upon India is set to host an immersive Sufi Qawwali Mehfil in Kolkata on Sunday, 29
articles.body: Bringing the richness of India’s musical heritage to the city, Once Upon India is set to host an immersive Sufi Qawwali Mehfil in Kolkata on Sunday, 29 November 2026.Celebrating the timeless appeal of Sufi music, the evening promises an evocative blend of soulful melodies, poetic expression and shared musical experiences. Drawing inspiration from legendary Sufi poets and musicians such as Amir Khusrau, Bulleh Shah and Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, the mehfil will take audiences on a journey through a musical tradition deeply rooted in devotion, love and spirituality.The highlight of the evening will be a special performance by the KM Sufi Ensemble from A.R. Rahman’s KM Music Conservatory. Featuring 20 trained musicians, the two-hour live presentation will bring together powerful vocals, harmonium, tabla and the distinctive rhythms of traditional qawwali. The repertoire will include much-loved devotional compositions by A.R. Rahman, including Kun Faya Kun, alongside timeless classics associated with Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. Adding another dimension to the experience, stories and insights behind the poetry and compositions will help audiences connect with the deeper meaning of the music.After captivating audiences in Delhi, Gurgaon, Mumbai and Bengaluru, the Sufi Qawwali Mehfil now arrives in Kolkata as part of its five-city India Tour 2026. The tour will also travel to Pune, Delhi and Jaipur, taking this celebration of India's musical traditions to audiences across the country.Founded in 2024 as an intimate home baithak, Once Upon India has grown into a cultural movement that helps audiences experience and reconnect with the soul of India. Through thoughtfully curated musical evenings, storytelling and immersive cultural experiences, the platform continues to celebrate India's living cultural traditions. articles.title: ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya’ Twitter review: Netizens rave about the new family drama and Sooraj Barjatya’s work - Says the movie is ‘a reminder that family, love, traditions, and relationships still matter’
articles.summary: Discover what audiences are saying about 'Yeh Prem Mol Liya', a new family drama featuring Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari. The film challenges traditional marriage norms and highlights the importance of family and relationships.
articles.body: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari’s latest film, ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya,' is officially here, and netizens and moviegoers have already started sharing their opinions about the movie online. Turning around the conventional take on marriage and how the woman always has to leave her home, ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya’ had already created quite a buzz for the unlikely pairing along with the fresh concept. Read ahead to learn more about what people think of the film.What is the plot of ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya’?The family drama film follows the story of Prem, who is played by Ayushmann Khurrana, who falls deeply for Purva, who is played by Sharvari. When Purva, who only has women in her family, says that she cannot leave her home for marriage, Prem agrees to move into her ancestral home along with his entire family, directly challenging social and cultural norms. Purva works as a journalist who is the only support system for the six women in her ancestral home, while Prem works as a musician and aspiring music director.Other than the two leading stars, the film has also cast Anupam Kher, Seema Pahwa, Supriya Pathak, Swanand Kirkire, Saumya Tandon, Geeta Agrawal Sharma, Shaad Randhawa, Shruti Seth, Rajesh Kumar, Girish Kulkarni, Jameel Khan, and many others.Netizens react to ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya’ on its release dayOne netizen wrote, “Two songs are ruling the charts this week: ‘Tu Mil Jaaye’ from King and the title track of Yeh Prem Mol Liya." Two different genres, and both penned by Kumaar. The man behind countless hits and always flying under the radar," while another social media user added that they liked the film; however, they had one complaint. They wrote in their post, “My only complaint is how rushed the romance feels...Ayushmann’s character proposes marriage to Sharvari’s character on the very first day they actually have a conversation...Sooraj ji...2 3 din ya ek aadh hafta toh ghumne firne dete ek doosre ko janne dete...fir propose karwate bhai…” (Sooraj-ji...you should have let them spend a few days or even a week just hanging out and getting to know each other...and then proposed, brother!)Another netizen commented, “There’s something beautiful about Sooraj Barjatya presenting a true Bollywood musical: a dead genre when most movies present songs as montages, remixes, and do the one odd item song!” Another fan called it the “detox” that 2026 needed all this time, further sharing, “In the indigestion of Jawans & Pathans, #YehPremMolLiya is a detox that forces you to pause, breathe & relive what Sooraj Barjatya universe stands for. I don't remember when we last saw the camera stay on close-ups to let actors act! Let's go back to "parivarik cinema." We need one in 2026.”Another social media user reviewed the film and commented, “#YehPremMolLiya is a reminder that family, love, traditions, and relationships still matter. A clean, feel-good entertainer that touches your heart and celebrates the goodness of human emotions. Superb performances, soulful music with a message.”Sooraj Barjatya directed the family drama film, while Himesh Reshammiya composed the music for ‘Yeh Prem Mol Liya.’Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Allu Aravind foresaw changing audience tastes towards pan-India films; was Allu Arjun aware of his prediction?
articles.summary: Prominent producer Allu Aravind, father of Tollywood star Allu Arjun is currently basking in the success of his latest release ‘Aakasamlo Oka Tara’ led by
articles.body: Prominent producer Allu Aravind, father of Tollywood star Allu Arjun is currently basking in the success of his latest release ‘Aakasamlo Oka Tara’ led by Dulquer Salmaan. Recently, the filmmaker spoke about the changing audience preferences towards big-budget pan-India films, recalling how he had anticipated a shift in audience interest towards such projects two years ago.Allu Aravind talks predicting the trendDuring a press meet in Hyderabad on Thursday, a reporter pointed out that several top Telugu stars are currently focusing on ambitious pan-India films. However, audiences have reportedly started showing interest in films that are more classy and pleasant to watch as quoted by Hindustan Times.Responding to the observation, Allu Aravind smiled and said, “Any good businessman can imagine what is happening after two to three years. Take my answer as me predicting what would happen two years ago, too.”Allu Aravind talks about commercial cinemaAllu Aravind also stated that his comments should not be seen as a prediction that commercial films would lose their appeal. He said he continues to believe in commercial cinema and is also working towards making such films.“I have said this to anybody in general. This is not to say that two years back I predicted that so-called commercial cinema would see lower reception. It is also my effort to make commercial films. I don’t know if my future films will be the way you described. But in 2027 and 2028, I will be backing films with a huge star cast that will become blockbusters.”During the interaction, the reporter also asked whether he had shared the prediction with Allu Arjun. He then laughed and replied, “Not really.”Allu Arjun’s upcoming filmAllu Arjun was last seen in the 2024 blockbuster pan-India film ‘Pushpa 2: The Rule’ directed by Sukumar. The film went on to make over Rs. 1,742.10 crore worldwide. Now, he is working on his next big budget sci-fi project ‘Raaka’ with director Atlee.He also has a tentatively titled ‘AA23’ with filmmaker Lokesh Kanagaraj in the pipeline.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
